name: Dior Omotesando
features: Clear glass skin over wavy translucent acrylic; floors of varied height read as white bands.
note: Flagship store; SANAA designed the shell, interiors were later refitted by Peter Marino (2014).

name: Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art
features: Row of storehouse-like roofs; materials rise from stone to tile to aluminium round an empty circular plaza.
commons_category: Category:Hiroshima City Museum of Contemporary Art

photos.file: File:広島市現代美術館 - panoramio.jpg

note: Completed 1988, opened 1989, in Hijiyama Park. The circular void and its roof opening point towards the hypocentre; some stone comes from the bombed city hall.

name: Kirishima International Concert Hall (Miyama Conseru)
features: Shoebox hall bent into a leaf-shaped plan with a keel-like section for sound, set in open hill country.
note: Main hall seats about 770. Home of the Kirishima International Music Festival.

name: Kumamoto Prefectural Museum of Art
features: Low brick-tiled galleries in the castle park grounds, with a deep coffered concrete ceiling and glass lobby.
note: Only one large exterior photo of the main building (CC0); File:Kumamoto-Prefectural Museum of Art main 1.jpg (800x450, CC BY-SA 3.0) is a second, small one. The category also holds good interior photos (lobby, coffered ceiling) and the separate annex by Martínez Lapeña-Torres, which is not this building. Wikipedia names no architect in the text; the Commons file description and the category give Maekawa.

name: Lee Ufan Museum
features: Half-buried in a valley between hills and sea; long concrete walls lead visitors in to the galleries.
award: Japanese contemporary: Tadao Ando public works

photos.file: File:Lee U-Fan museum 李禹煥美術館 香川県香川郡直島町字倉浦 PC192966.jpg
File:Lee U-Fan museum 李禹煥美術館 香川県香川郡直島町字倉浦 PC192974.jpg
File:Lee U-Fan museum 李禹煥美術館 香川県香川郡直島町字倉浦 PC192991.jpg

note: Designed with the artist Lee Ufan. Many photos also show his sculptures in the forecourt.

name: Matsumoto Performing Arts Centre
features: Curving walls of GRC panels set with about 20,000 glass pieces that speckle light inside and out.
note: Main hall 1,800 seats, small hall 240. Structural engineer Mutsuro Sasaki.

name: Mikimoto Ginza 2
features: Pale pink walls of concrete poured between steel plates carry the floors; irregular windows are cut at random.
note: Column-free: the four thin steel-and-concrete walls form the structure (engineer Mutsuro Sasaki).

name: Museum of Modern Art, Saitama
features: A glass entrance hall set inside a deep concrete grid frame, opening the museum into Kitaurawa Park.

photos.file: File:The Museum of Modern Art, Saitama.jpg
File:埼玉県立近代美術館 - panoramio.jpg

note: Kurokawa's first art museum; opened November 1982. Known as MOMAS.

name: Nagoya City Art Museum
features: Kept below the height of the park's trees; galleries lie underground, lit by a sunken garden.

photos.file: File:Nagoya City Art Museum 01, Sakae Naka Ward Nagoya 2020.jpg

note: Completed 1987, opened April 1988, in Shirakawa Park. Plan set on a north-south main axis; Kurokawa drew on traditional Japanese forms and local motifs.

name: National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto
features: Granite and glass facade ruled by a 1.5 m grid, with glazed corner stair towers, facing Okazaki Park.
commons_category: Category:National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto

photos.file: File:National Museum of Modern Art Kyoto 2010.jpg
File:The National Museum of Modern Art, Kyoto.jpg
File:National Museum of Modern Art (Kyoto Sakyo-ku) hdsr S5 01.jpg

name: Nissay Theatre (Nippon Life Hibiya Building)
features: Stone-clad block facing Hibiya Park; inside, a hall with no straight lines and 20,000 pearl shells overhead.

photos.file: File:Nippon Life Insurance Company (Nihon Seimei Hibiya Bldg.).jpg

note: Built 1960-63 for Nippon Life's 70th anniversary; opened 1963. Wikipedia does not name the facade stone, so the features line keeps to stone-clad (as the photos show).

name: Odate Jukai Dome
features: Egg-shaped dome of about 25,000 Akita cedar members under a double Teflon membrane that sheds snow.
note: Now called Nipro Hachiko Dome. About 178 x 157 m in plan, 52 m high. Sources call the timber Akita cedar or Akita cypress.

name: Osaka Prefectural Sayamaike Museum
features: Concrete courts of water: visitors pass beneath a wall of falling water to reach a hall cut through the old dam.
award: Japanese contemporary: Tadao Ando public works
note: Displays a section of the ancient Sayamaike reservoir dam. Two photos are 1280x720 (the only good views of the water court).

name: Kadokawa Culture Museum
features: Angular polyhedron clad in 20,000 granite plates, as if rock had broken up through the ground; 8 m bookshelf theatre.

photos.file: File:Kadokawa Culture Museum at Tokorozawa Sakura Town (50608208297).jpg

note: With Kajima Design; core of the Tokorozawa Sakura Town complex. Opened November 2020.

name: Kurashiki Ivy Square
features: Meiji-era brick spinning mill turned into a hotel and halls; part cleared for a plaza paved with its old tiles.

photos.file: File:211203 Kurashiki Ivy Square Kurashiki Okayama pref Japan10s3.jpg
File:211203 Kurashiki Ivy Square Kurashiki Okayama pref Japan03s3.jpg
File:211203 Kurashiki Ivy Square Kurashiki Okayama pref Japan02s3.jpg

note: Former Kurashiki Spinning Works (1889). Ivy was planted in the factory era to keep the buildings cool. Some sources spell the architect Shintaro Urabe. The white wooden building in many photos is a separate older building on the site.

name: National Museum of Japanese History
features: Long, low museum on the Sakura Castle ruins, entered across a broad brick forecourt under a vaulted canopy.
note: Building dated 1980 by Ashihara's office; the museum opened 16 March 1983. The features line is drawn from the photos (forecourt and entrance canopy); no source describes the design in detail.

name: Shinjuku Park Tower
features: Three linked towers of 52, 47 and 41 storeys stepping down in height, each topped by a glazed pyramid.
note: 235 m tall. The Park Hyatt Tokyo occupies the top floors. The three pointed roofs are named in a Commons file description; Wikipedia only says three connected blocks.

name: Embassy of Kuwait, Tokyo
features: Block-like concrete volumes stacked asymmetrically round a raised courtyard: chancery below, residence above.
note: Seven storeys. A 2017 plan to rebuild it was reported; SOS Brutalism says it still stands and is in use.

name: Komazawa Olympic Park Control Tower and Gymnasium
features: A 50 m concrete tower of stacked slab tiers, a modern pagoda, rising from a raised plaza beside the gymnasium.
note: Built for the 1964 Olympics (wrestling in the gymnasium). Wikipedia credits Ashihara with both gymnasium and tower; one blog credits the tower to Masachika Murata, so authorship of the tower is not fully settled. Category:Komazawa Gymnasium mixes in photos of the later indoor ball-games hall (the arched building), so photos were taken from the tower category, where the first file shows both.

name: Miyagi Stadium
features: Stadium turned into a hill in the landscape, under a crescent roof recalling Date Masamune's helmet.
note: Only one usable exterior photo (1600x1200); other files are interior views of the stands, which also show the crescent roof. A cropped copy exists (File:MiyagiStadium2007-4-29 cropped.jpg). 2002 World Cup venue.

name: Toyota Stadium
features: Curved roofs hung by cables from four giant masts, so no columns block the view; massive concrete piers below.
note: Engineered with Arup Japan. Its retractable membrane roof has been fixed since 2015 and was to be replaced by a fixed canopy.

name: NOA Building
features: A near-windowless dark oval tower rising from a low red-brick drum: 15 storeys of office.
note: 61.75 m. Sources disagree on the cladding of the oval upper part (copper per Wikipedia, steel per Architecture Tokyo), so the features line says dark only.

name: United Nations University Headquarters
features: Symmetrical stepped tower on Aoyama-dori, narrowing like a ziggurat to a pointed glass top, with a front plaza.
note: Handed over by the Japanese government on 30 June 1992; inaugurated 17 February 1993. Wikipedia names Tange but does not describe the form: the features line is from the photos.

name: Onagawa Station
features: White membrane roof like a seabird's spread wings over a timber lattice; a public hot-spring bath upstairs.

photos.file: File:JR East Onagawa Station building, Miyagi Pref 20240420.jpg
File:JR East Onagawa Station building, Miyagi Pref.jpg

note: Rebuilt after the 2011 tsunami, inland and on raised ground. Bath tiles painted by Hiroshi Senju. The two chosen photos are near-identical front views; the rest of the category is mostly platform and sign shots.

name: Sakaide Artificial Ground
features: A concrete deck 6 to 9 m up carries public housing and a new ground; shops, halls and parking sit beneath.
note: Built in phases 1963-1978 (1968 is the date of the Pompidou model and first phase). Partly deteriorating; residents are ageing.

name: Shonandai Cultural Center
features: Architecture as second nature: halls buried below a plaza of cosmic spheres, small metal roofs and a stream.
note: First public competition in Japan won by a woman architect; designed with residents' participation.

name: Shoto Museum of Art
features: Curved wall of rough Korean granite under a bronze-louvred eave; galleries round a deep light well with fountains.
note: Completed May 1980, opened October 1981. Height limit of 10 m, so two floors are underground.

name: Takanawa Gateway Station
features: Folded, origami-like roof of steel and laminated timber under a translucent membrane, like shoji screens.
note: Opened March 2020 on the Yamanote Line; photos are from the full opening of the surrounding district.

name: Gunma Music Center
features: Thin folded-plate concrete roof and walls zigzag over the hall, funded partly by citizens' donations.
note: Co-designed with Ladislav Rado. Built on the site of Takasaki Castle. Raymond was Czech-American, working in Japan.

name: Kasumigaseki Building
features: Japan's first modern skyscraper, 36 floors on a flexible steel frame built to ride out earthquakes.
note: 147 m. Flexible structure by Kiyoshi Muto; made possible by the end of the 31 m height limit. Wikipedia lists Kajima as architect; Yamashita Sekkei and Shinkenchiku credit Yamashita (Kajima built it).

name: Kabuki-za (2013)
features: The old theatre face rebuilt with its karahafu gables and reused stone and ornament, an office tower rising behind.
note: Fifth Kabuki-za, reopened April 2013; the tower (Kabukiza Tower, 29 floors) bridges over the column-free theatre. Designed with Mitsubishi Jisho Sekkei. It continues the look of Isoya Yoshida's 1950s rebuild.

name: Yatsushiro Municipal Museum
features: Galleries hidden under a grassy mound; above, light billowing roofs and a floating half-cylinder store.
note: Kumamoto Artpolis project. Only one photo on Commons (2500x2000, CC BY-SA 3.0). The mound was raised because high groundwater ruled out a basement.

name: Inter-University Seminar House
features: Main hall is an inverted concrete pyramid driven into the hillside; seminar and lodging huts scatter over the slope.
note: Yoshizaka worked for Le Corbusier 1950-52. The main hall is a Tokyo-selected historic building. Commons also has good photos of the auditorium, library and unit houses.

name: Athénée Français
features: French language school whose walls, in deep purple and pink, carry small relief marks and rise to a tower.
note: Wikipedia dates it 1962; Yoshizaka's archive dates the project 1960-81 (extensions). Won an AIJ Prize. No written source describes the facade, so the features line follows the two photos; worth checking before use.

name: Museum of Modern Art, Kamakura (Kamakura Bunkakan Tsurugaoka Museum)
features: Light box of galleries on slender pilotis reaching over Heike Pond, round a central courtyard.
commons_category: Category:The Museum of Modern Art, Kamakura

photos.file: File:The Museum of Modern Art, Kamakura 2009.jpg

note: Japan's first public museum of modern art. The museum left in 2016; the building passed to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu and reopened as Kamakura Bunkakan Tsurugaoka Museum. Important Cultural Property; DOCOMOMO Japan.

name: Meguro City Office (former Chiyoda Life Insurance HQ)
features: Long office blocks screened by modular cast-aluminium louvres, wrapped round a sunken Japanese garden.
note: Built as Chiyoda Life Insurance headquarters; converted to the city office with minimal changes in 2003. Interiors (stairs, tea house) are notable.

name: Nippon Budokan
features: Octagonal hall modelled on the Yumedono of Horyu-ji, its sweeping roof meant to recall Mount Fuji, topped by a giboshi.

photos.file: File:Nippon Budokan - sunny day - Nov 12 2021 various.jpeg

note: Built for judo at the 1964 Olympics (October 1963 to September 1964). Criticised at the time as too traditional, next to Yamada's modernist Kyoto Tower.

name: Kyoto Tower
features: A white candle of welded steel rings and plate, no lattice, standing on a nine-storey hotel block by Kyoto Station.
note: 131 m to the spire; observation deck at 100 m. Structural advice from Makoto Tanahashi. Controversial in its day in historic Kyoto.

name: Toyoda Auditorium, Nagoya University
features: A concrete frame with modules set into it, opening as a deep gateway onto the campus lawn.

photos.file: File:名古屋大学の豊田講堂(20210718).jpg

note: Gift of Toyota to the university, 1960. Restored and extended by Maki in 2008; Registered Tangible Cultural Property 2011, the first so registered in its designer's lifetime.

name: Shizuoka Convention and Arts Center (Granship)
features: A great hull-shaped hall clad in dark scale-like stone, with a glazed, arched bow and a tower behind.
note: Isozaki's largest project at the time: large hall (concerts and sport), drama hall, convention area. No written source describes the form; the features line follows the photos, and a Commons file names the cladding as Lugo green phyllite.

name: Nagi Museum of Contemporary Art
features: Three galleries, Sun, Moon and Earth, each built around one permanent artwork and set to its orientation.
note: Sun: tilted cylinder by Arakawa and Madeline Gins; Moon: Kazuo Okazaki, a straight wall and shallow arc aimed at the autumn moon; Earth: Aiko Miyawaki. Only one Commons photo (2048x1536).

name: Mt. Fuji World Heritage Centre, Shizuoka
features: Inverted cone of hinoki timber lattice over a pool, whose reflection completes the shape of Mount Fuji.
note: Opened December 2017. A 193 m spiral ramp climbs inside the cone; steel truss shell clad in local cypress.

name: Za-Koenji Public Theatre
features: Tent-like dark steel-plate concrete shell, its roof carved by cones and cylinders, pricked with small glazed portholes.

photos.file: File:ZA-Koenji, Suginami 座・高円寺 Jun 28, 2026.jpg

note: Suginami Art Center is the Commons category name. Sources give 2008 or 2009 for completion; opened May 2009.

name: Aore Nagaoka City Hall
features: City hall and arena round a covered earth-floored plaza, the nakadoma, walled in chequered wood and solar panels.
note: Brings the city hall back to the town centre beside the station. The plaza floor uses tataki, a traditional rammed-earth finish.

name: Starbucks Coffee, Dazaifu Tenmangu Omotesando
features: About 2,000 slim cedar sticks woven diagonally, four meeting at each joint, fill a narrow shopfront.

photos.file: File:スターバックス 太宰府天満宮表参道店 (31824610824).jpg

note: A small shop on the approach to Dazaifu Tenmangu shrine; opened December 2011. Sticks 6 cm square, 1.3 to 4 m long.

name: The Prince Kyoto Takaragaike (Kyoto Takaragaike Prince Hotel)
features: Ring-shaped hotel: 310 rooms along one corridor round a garden court, the rounded tiers stepping back.

photos.file: File:宝ヶ池プリンスホテル.jpg

note: One of Murano's last works (he died in 1984; opened October 1986). Sources are mainly the hotel's own pages.

name: Japan Pavilion, Venice Biennale
features: Square gallery box raised on four massive pilotis, one per side; a floor opening and glass-block ceiling bring light.
note: No usable exterior photo: the category holds an installation view, a signboard, and File:Japanese pavilion at the Venice biennial.jpg (1200x1800, CC BY-SA 3.0), which shows only one corner under a tree. Italy has no freedom of panorama for buildings and Yoshizaka died in 1980, so photos may be deleted. Not drawn: sources give the raised box on four pilotis, but I could not pin down the facade pattern, the entrance stair or the sloping ground well enough. Restored under Toyo Ito in 2014. Co-author Juichi Otake per archiweb.

name: Hotel Tokoen
features: Concrete columns and beams read as a torii; upper floors hang from 7th-floor beams over an open garden floor.
note: No Commons category; both files were found by search (described as Kikutake, Hotel Tokoen, 1964). The second is 1036x1528, which is under 1200px on its long side but over 800. Gardens and bathhouse by sculptor Masayuki Nagare. At Kaike Onsen.

name: Miyakonojo Civic Hall
features: Hall roofed by a great fan of steel ribs rising from a concrete base; a Metabolist landmark, demolished 2019-20.
note: Demolished 2019-2020 after closing in 2007 (most residents polled agreed); 3D-scanned before demolition. The fan-of-ribs description follows the photos; written sources do not describe the roof. Include only if the wall takes lost buildings.

name: Shiroiya Hotel
features: A renovated 1970s hotel paired with a new Green Tower: a grassy mound planted with shrubs and trees.
note: Only one Commons file (2000x1500, CC BY 4.0, from the north, showing the Green Tower), found by search; there is no category. Artist rooms and an atrium work by Leandro Erlich are inside the Heritage Tower.
